groups.test: restores keyboard focus and honors reduced motion
groups.reason: Desktop keyboard behavior is exercised on both desktop engines; touch behavior has its own mobile case.

groups.test: has no serious or critical automated accessibility findings
groups.reason: Axe is the single canonical DOM audit; keyboard, reflow, touch, and semantic checks cover the other profiles independently.

groups.test: supports the complete touch journey, local share, and follow exit
groups.reason: This is the dedicated Pixel 7 touch-profile case; both desktop projects run the full pointer/keyboard journey elsewhere.

groups.test: preserves semantics through context loss, tab resume, and orientation
groups.reason: The desktop resume/context-loss matrix runs on both browser engines; mobile orientation and journey behavior are exercised by the touch case.

groups.test: remains legible with forced colors and 200 percent text
groups.reason: Forced-colors emulation is the canonical Chromium audit; narrow mobile reflow is separately exercised at 390 by 844.

groups.test: keeps the production browser boundary local and restrictive
groups.reason: The same static production document and CSP serve every engine, so one canonical network-boundary capture avoids duplicating an engine-independent assertion.

browserCoverage.chromium: complete journey, fallback, deterministic semantics, accessibility, resilience, reflow, and security
browserCoverage.webkit: complete journey, fallback, deterministic semantics, keyboard, and resilience
browserCoverage.mobileChromium: complete touch journey at a Pixel 7 profile
browserCoverage.firefox: Not installed on the validation machine and not counted as passed; Chromium plus WebKit satisfy the required local cross-engine smoke matrix.
